post_content:
Let me be honest. I was jealous. Until a few months back, I was jealous of the
people who had thousands of followers and hundreds of interactions on their
posts on hashtag#LinkedIn. I was jealous because I believed that these are
people who get work literally thrown into their laps. But then, all of this
perception changed when I got an opportunity to interact with one such person.
Look at my shock when he came to me to inquire if I had any hashtag#freelance
work for him! I started talking and realized the numbers don't matter on
LinkedIn! Having a few likes on quality posts with four valuable leads in the
inbox triumphs over hundreds of likes and countless irrelevant messages. I'm
now content with what I have and wouldn't, for the love of God, exchange what
I got with that of these LinkedIn 'popular figures'! hashtag#linkedinlife
hashtag#linkedincreators hashtag#posts

Just read a report on The Hindu which says "Indian demands for content removal
on Twitter is fourth highest in the world " Now, when I went to data, they are
measuring absolute counts of all cases for content removal. My question is why
aren't they normalized ? Each country has different amount of population and
different active uses. For example, number of cases for content removal per
million active users might be a better idea so that we can infer better
information. What say ? Ankit Rathi Amit Choudhary Srivatsan Srinivasan
